title: `resources/read`
description: Reads the contents behind a resource URI, which may return several contents for one request.
question: Can the agent read a resource's contents through the framework?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Listing resources without reading them is a catalogue with no way to open anything. This row is where the primitive becomes usable, and it is also where a framework that returns only the first of several contents starts losing data.

notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: a text resource is returned as a bare string. The contents arrive intact, but the `uri` and `mimeType` that identify them are dropped, so the agent cannot tell which resource it just read.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `resources/read` is unreachable.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ReadResource` on.
